title: Answer a counting question with zero digit characters
rationale: Digit bans are used for redaction and speech-friendly text; models echo numerals out of habit, which defeats the constraint and slips past downstream digit filtering.

prompt.content: You are a terse assistant. Answer only with the requested word; spell out all numbers and never explain.
How many legs does a spider have? Write the count using English words and make sure your entire reply contains no digits.

notes: Deterministic: static prompt, temperature 0, whole-response digit anchor. Brittleness: a correct answer such as 'Spiders have eight legs.' passes while 'Eight (8)' fails by design; the positive unit requires the word eight, not the numeral.
